components.html:
Full context & responsibilities+

The client, one of the largest globally recognized German automotive manufacturers, commissioned a custom market research analytics platform to uncover why specific customer segments prefer particular products and inform targeted marketing and production strategies. The platform combined automated data ingestion from sources like SPSS files, a research-oriented data warehouse supporting longitudinal analysis, and cross-tabulation tools for exploring behavioral patterns and trends. My work covered the visualization layer.

I translated approximately 15 sketch-based designs into fully functional Tableau dashboards, working with datasets prepared by the data engineering team for each market research use case. Each dashboard went through iterative review cycles where I submitted completed work, the client provided feedback, and I refined until function and visuals matched both the original sketches and the client's expectations. The dashboards were then embedded into the client's internal portal as part of the platform's enterprise integration.

In parallel, I conducted R&D on Tableau Extensions to evaluate how third-party visual components could accelerate future development, offer richer chart types, and reduce reliance on complex calculated fields, simplifying both knowledge transfer and long-term maintenance.

Responsibilities

  • Built the Tableau visualization layer for a custom market research analytics platform
  • Translated ~15 sketch-based designs into production Tableau dashboards end-to-end
  • Worked with datasets prepared by the data engineering team across multiple market research use cases
  • Iterated through multiple client review cycles to align function and visuals with expectations
  • Researched Tableau Extensions to expand visual options and simplify long-term maintenance
  • Coordinated with the embedding team on technical constraints and integration readiness

Impact

Delivered the full dashboard suite for the platform, live and embedded in the client's internal portal, enabling cross-tabulation and longitudinal analysis of customer behavior to support targeted marketing and production decisions.

narrative.overview:
Precise, capable, and visually curious. Data organized into a useful system is the established metaphor: large sans-serif propositions, explicit evidence, open reading surfaces, and short motion that organizes existing marks. “Inside the decision” is the subordinate case-reading pattern; it does not introduce a second identity.

Celadon + ink remains the approved palette. The interface is spacious at the level of a section and compact at the level of a fact. Filled pills, ruled rows, and geometric evidence distinguish actions, records, and illustrations. The previous repeated serif-room compositions and floating glass navigation are superseded. No gradients, ornamental glow, or fabricated interface chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Evidence quantities and qualifiers stay readable independently of graphics.
Celadon surfaces and green accents pair with decisive DM Sans; DM Mono is reserved for brief metadata.
Flat sections, hairline dividers, square evidence panels, and rounded actions establish hierarchy.
Short evidence sequences resolve to still reading states; deliberate pointer feedback remains available.
System-following light and dark palettes preserve the same identity and information.

rules.name: The Foreground Pair Rule
rules.body: Switch foreground and background together. Theme changes are immediate; do not animate one color across the other or invert screenshot pixels.

rules.name: The Evidence Never Drops Rule
rules.body: Exact values, labels, and qualifiers remain readable at narrow widths and at browser zoom. Only a redundant graphic may be omitted, never the evidence it represents.

rules.name: The Flat Reading Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep ordinary reading content flat. Use the existing preview shadow only for the decorative panel that sits above it.

rules.name: The Reconstruction Is Explicit Rule
rules.body: The governance artwork says “Count illustration, not an access map.” Other evidence graphics derive from typed quantities, named sources, or delivery tracks. They do not imply a real schema, formal artifact, or unknown measurement. Approximate and minimum figures retain their `~` or `+` labels.

dos: Do use semantic theme pairs and retain the approved Celadon + ink identity.
Do keep exact evidence values, labels, and `~` / `+` qualifiers readable at every width.
Do distinguish illustrative geometry from client topology and keep prototype provenance beside the screenshots.
Do reuse the shared header, hash-linked case reader, focus restoration, and existing image viewer.
Do preserve reduced-motion, forced-colors, touch, keyboard, and no-JavaScript paths.
Do edit substantive copy in data and keep generated reading editions equivalent.
donts: Don't restore the superseded serif-room typography, oxblood palette, or floating glass navigation.
Don't add gradients, ornamental glow, client names or logos, fabricated screenshots, testimonials, or unverified metrics.
Don't imply that the manufacturing prototype used real client data or shipped to production.
Don't hide metric text to make a mobile layout fit or rely on a floating preview for essential information.
Don't apply screenshot inversion or hue rotation, or persist a manual theme choice across visits.
Don't describe local build/browser checks as deployment or real-device verification.
